decoded.axis: stop placement, and the "two stop options" veto
decoded.headline: Austin's stop is always anchored to a structural reference (the entry candle's body, the opening-range candle's body, or pivot structure) and never a bare price/fixed distance — and when two such references sit close together ("two stop options") the evidence shows a downgrade or a wait-for-a-cleaner-entry, not an automatic veto; a hard "no" only appeared when the stop-option complaint was compounded with a separate "level not respected" issue.

claims.claim: Of the 6 where_is_the_stop cards (answers B, C, none, A, C, none), both 'none' answers are refusals of the trade/entry itself (wrong timing or wrong setup) — not confusion between the 4 candidate stop prices. NFLX_2025-07-28 is rejected as too late in the day/mid-chop; SOFI_2025-11-07 is rejected because the offered entry isn't the one he'd take (he names 9:46 as 'the good trade' instead). Neither note discusses which of A/B/C/D looks like the right invalidation price.
claims.austin_quote: not an entry too late in the day trading between day chop
claims.codeable_form: IF stop_pick == 'none': classify as ENTRY_REJECTED (bad timing / wrong candle offered), route to the no-trade / entry-timing classifier — do NOT treat as an unresolved stop-selection case among A/B/C/D.

claims.claim: Where he states a stop rationale at all, the stop is pinned to a structural anchor — 'the candle entered on', the opening-range candle's body, or pivot structure — and any numeric adjustment he mentions elsewhere is a few-cents fine-tune around that anchor, never a standalone fixed-distance rule. Within the two assigned files this shows up explicitly on 2 of 6 where_is_the_stop cards plus 1 of 8 trade_anatomy cards (the only one graded wrong on 'stop'); it is heavily corroborated outside the assigned files (7 more instances in austin_marks_v7.jsonl / recovered_reviews.jsonl, e.g. 'stop a little lower at the lower body of the green one candle rule', 'lower the stop a couple cents maybe?') but those are cited as corroboration only, not counted in this claim's denominator.
claims.austin_quote: this and last one have been stop below the candle entered on.
claims.codeable_form: stop_price = structural_anchor_price(entry_candle_body_extreme | opening_range_candle_body_extreme | nearest_pivot) [+/- a few cents]; reject any candidate stop rule expressed as entry_price - fixed_$_or_point_offset with no structural anchor.

claims.claim: 'Two stop options' (his phrase: 'lots of close stop options' / '2 stop loss options') is a real, recurring critique across 3 different decks (is_this_an_s, deep_is_s, trade_anatomy) — but the 3 instances do not agree it is a hard veto. TSLA_2025-05-16 is explicitly still called 'A trade' (a downgrade from S, not a kill). PLTR_2024-10-23's fix is to wait 6 candles for the cleaner OCR entry, not to skip the day. Only META_2024-09-30 lands on an outright 'no', and that note pairs the stop-option complaint with a second, distinct complaint ('not respecting level') — so the veto-strength evidence is confounded, not clean.
claims.austin_quote: its hard to enter a stock when there 2 stop loss options and you wouldve stayed in the trade if you went with the OCR entry 6 candles later.
claims.codeable_form: AT candidate signal time: stop_refs = {nearby structural stop anchors (candle-body extremes / pivots) within an as-yet-uncalibrated proximity band of the primary anchor}. IF len(stop_refs) >= 2: downgrade one grade (S->A) by default, OR (preferred per PLTR_2024-10-23) defer entry until price action collapses stop_refs to 1 (e.g. wait for the OCR retest). Full veto (no_trade) only IF additionally level_respected == False — this combination is untested as an independent factor and needs more cards before shipping as a standalone veto.

claims.claim: 'i dont like bodies' appears exactly once in the two assigned files, as a hedge inside a sentence that then concedes the body-based stop would have been better anyway. This reads as in tension with (not obviously the same claim as) Austin's own routine elsewhere of pricing stops at a candle's upper/lower body — but that routine practice comes from other corpora, outside this axis's assigned files, so the tension is noted, not resolved. Separately: nothing here conflicts with the repo's settled close-trigger/wicks-stop-nothing rule — a body-edge stop (open/close level) is exactly the kind of price a close-based stop test evaluates against, so a candle-body stop reference and a close-trigger fill rule are complementary, not competing.
claims.austin_quote: those 3 green candles even though i dont like bodies that wouldve been a better stop.
claims.codeable_form: NOT-CODEABLE from this evidence alone. Do not encode a general 'avoid candle-body stops' rule — this is one hedge on one card, and it does not name what alternative he'd have preferred instead of the body. Needs a direct question to Austin.

unsupported_questions: Is 'two stop options' ever a standalone veto (no trade) on its own, or does it always require a second problem (like 'level not respected') to actually kill the trade? All 3 cards found point different directions (downgrade / wait for a cleaner entry / one compounded 'no') and none isolates the stop-option factor alone.
What is the proximity threshold for 'two stop options' — is there a cents/percent tolerance like the zero-tolerance retest rule (g87), or is it purely an eye-test judgment with no fixed unit?

In NVDA_2024-09-03, what does 'i dont like bodies' actually refer to — a general aversion to body-based stops (which would contradict his routine body-anchored stops seen elsewhere), or something specific to that chart (e.g. he'd have preferred a wick or a level instead)?

For the two 'none' answers in where_is_the_stop (NFLX_2025-07-28, SOFI_2025-11-07), should a future stop-pick UI even offer 4 stop-price choices when the real answer is 'this isn't the entry' — i.e. should entry-validity be asked before stop-selection, not folded into the same question?

decoded.headline: Displacement is real, load-bearing vocabulary Austin uses unprompted across ~20 cards to justify S-vs-A entry grading, but the one probe section built specifically to test it (8 cards, all "no") is broken — zero contrast cases, and Austin himself flagged he couldn't trust it — so those 8 rows measure the deck, not him; the one usable signal from that section is his own definition sentence on card 8.

claims.claim: The dedicated 8-card 'displacement' probe section returned an identical answer ("no") on 8/8 cards, with notes filled in on only 1 of 8 — and on that 8th card Austin explicitly says the pattern is making him doubt the probe, not just the charts. This is evidence the probe section is broken (no contrast/'yes' cases were ever shown, so it never tested whether he CAN recognize displacement), not evidence about his judgment.
claims.austin_quote: displaced and closed into the levels at 9:45, but these past 8 make me anxious you cant remember what it means. just one candle closes away and displaces itsself from other candles in some form, and the level in question
claims.codeable_form: NOT-CODEABLE AS A TRADING RULE — this is a finding about instrument design, not price action. Predicate: probe_section_is_diagnostic(section) := section contains at least one positive AND one negative labeled example. The displacement section fails this (8/8 negative), so any per-card variance (or lack of it) inside it cannot be attributed to Austin's concept of displacement.

claims.claim: Austin's own definition of displacement, stated once, in reaction to the broken probe: a single candle (read by us as the signal/entry candle) both (a) closes decisively away from — i.e. stands apart from — the immediately preceding cluster of candles, and (b) does so relative to the specific level being tested, with no fixed metric for how far/how many candles.
claims.austin_quote: just one candle closes away and displaces itsself from other candles in some form, and the level in question
claims.codeable_form: is_displaced(c, level, lookback=N) := (c.close is beyond `level` in the trade direction — a decisive close through the level, not a wick-only touch) AND (c's range/body does not meaningfully overlap the range of the preceding N candles, i.e. c visually separates from that recent cluster). MY INFERENCES, not his words: (1) 'one candle' = the signal/entry candle specifically, not any candle in the sequence — inferred from how the term is used elsewhere ('9:46 ... no displacement', tied to a specific entry minute); (2) the comparison set 'other candles' = a small lookback (I guessed N=3-5) based on his separate '2 candle distraction' language on NFLX_2025-05-07; (3) the non-overlap/'stands apart' mechanism for 'in some form' is a guess — he explicitly declines to give a metric, and that refusal echoes his refusal on retest tolerance ('you stress test and find the best metric yourself', rule_01 ballot) — so a hardcoded threshold here is an engineering choice he never made, not a rule extracted from him.

claims.claim: In at least 5 cards, spontaneously (not inside the dedicated probe), 'no displacement' is the explicit stated reason an entry gets graded 'A' (his ladder) rather than S — the clearest is ACHR_2025-06-27, where he grades the whole card S but explicitly attributes it to a LATER entry, and downgrades the earlier entry to A by name because it lacks displacement.
claims.austin_quote: 9:39 A entry no displacement, S entry at 10
claims.codeable_form: downgrade_to_A(entry) := is_S_candidate(entry) AND NOT is_displaced(entry.candle, entry.level) — used as a NECESSARY condition for the entry-level downgrade in these 5 instances. n_relevant=113 is every card outside the dedicated displacement section where an individual entry's quality is discussed in prose (take_the_trade=39 + deep_is_s=60 + is_this_an_s=8 + htf_agree=6); 5/113 is a real but sparse signal — call this a hint, not a rule, per house rule against overselling.

claims.claim: In a broader set of 6 cards, 'no displacement' (or the structured why_not:no_displacement tag) is cited as a reason the whole card is NOT an S / not worth taking, without specifying A vs C.
claims.austin_quote: long entry has no displacement so not S unless you knew
claims.codeable_form: not_S(card) := ... no_displacement is one of the cited reasons (sometimes alone — AMD_2025-12-23 structured why_not:['no_displacement'] — sometimes alongside chop/level_not_respected — HOOD_2024-11-15). NOT-CODEABLE precisely as a standalone gate: in 5 of these 6 it's paired with or ambiguous against other named problems (chop, pivot-not-level, poor structure), so it functions as one of several disqualifiers, not an isolated veto rule.

claims.claim: Direct contradiction, flagged by Austin himself: on AMZN_2025-11-21 he explicitly says his own displacement-based downgrade call contradicts what he said on a different AMZN card, and grades both entries A 'because of no displacement' anyway, on what he calls a 'range chop day of hell'.
claims.austin_quote: this ex contradicts what i said about 22 amzn, because two losers on either side 9:35, 9:41, but both A trades because of no displacement, but that was a range chop day of hell
claims.codeable_form: NOT-CODEABLE — this is Austin flagging his own rule application as inconsistent across two similar cards, in real time, inside the marks. It is evidence the displacement→A rule is applied with judgment/context (here: day regime, 'range chop') rather than mechanically, and that even he isn't fully confident it was applied the same way twice.

claims.claim: Resolution of the apparent S-vs-'no displacement' contradiction: displacement functions as a SUFFICIENT confluence for S, not a strictly NECESSARY one — on 2 cards graded S he explicitly writes 'no displacement' about the entry candle but immediately supplies a named alternate confluence (OCR hold, wick-reclaim-of-level confluence, or strong PA) as the substitute that earns the S anyway.
claims.austin_quote: 10:04 no displacement but holding ocr at 9:56 and strong PA above the candles earlier and in the wick of those levels
claims.codeable_form: is_S(entry) := is_displaced(entry) OR has_compensating_confluence(entry) where compensating_confluence in {ocr_hold, wick_reclaim_of_level, strong_PA_above_recent_candles}. n_relevant=5 = the S-graded deep_is_s cards where he discusses the entry's displacement status in prose at all (IWM_2026-05-12, AVGO_2025-02-20, ACHR_2025-06-27, NVDA_2025-06-03, PLTR_2025-07-17); 3 of the 5 show displacement present and consistent with the S grade, 2 of the 5 (counted here) show it explicitly absent yet still graded S via a named substitute — so displacement is the modal/default path to S, not the only one. NOT-CODEABLE precisely: no stated rule for how many substitute confluences are required, or whether they're weighted equally to displacement itself.

unsupported_questions: What exact lookback window ("other candles") and what metric ("in some form") define displacement numerically — he explicitly declines to give one, mirroring his refusal to give a retest-tolerance metric.
Is displacement evaluated only on the entry/signal candle, or can an earlier candle in the sequence satisfy it (NFLX_2025-05-07: "i belive displacement happens before")?
When displacement is absent, is there a minimum required combination of substitute confluences (OCR hold / wick reclaim / strong PA / HTF bias), or does any one of them suffice?

Is Jdub's rule_14 framing ("primary downgrade [from S to A] is no displacement and has a clear trend") something Austin wants shipped as a literal engine rule, or just agreement with the general shape of it in a ballot exercise?

Does 'diss' (AVGO_2025-02-20: "holds that one candle diss into it a little") mean displacement, or something else — the same card also uses the full word 'displacement' separately, so the two may not be synonyms.
Is the AMZN_2025-11-21 self-flagged contradiction resolved by day regime (his own explanation: 'range chop day of hell'), or is it simply inconsistent application that a codeable rule cannot capture?

decoded.headline: Where a comparable engine timestamp exists, Austin's named entry is earlier than the engine's in 10 of 12 cases (1 to 58 minutes earlier); the two apparent exceptions turn out to be a different question type or a different complaint (break-vs-retest), not a "too early" complaint — so the lateness asymmetry is total in the strict sense.

claims.claim: Strict, literal-timestamp deltas (his named minute vs. the engine's field in the SAME row): engine is later in all 7 cases. Deltas (his minus engine, minutes) = -2, -10, -3, -13, -58, -19, -1. Median = -10 min, mean = -15.1 min, range -58 to -1 (spread 57 min).

claims.codeable_form: For each row carrying both an engine timestamp field (setup_et/entry_et/dot_A_et/dot_B_et/et) and a literal clock-time Austin names as his entry: delta_min = austin_minute - engine_minute. Observed set: {TSM_2025-11-03: dot_B_et 09:46 vs 9:44 -> -2; HOOD_2025-12-23: setup_et 09:56 vs 9:46 -> -10; TSLA_2025-03-25: setup_et 09:43 vs 9:40 -> -3; MSFT_2026-08-10: entry_et 09:46 vs 9:33 -> -13; SOFI_2025-11-07: entry_et 10:44 vs 9:46 -> -58; GOOGL_2024-10-15: et 10:02 vs 9:43 -> -19; QQQ_2025-02-25: et 09:47 vs 9:46 -> -1}. n_relevant=34 is every row in the two files carrying an engine timestamp field at all (the pool that COULD have produced a comparable literal delta); only 7 did.

claims.claim: Adding the 4 cases where he states the offset in candle-count language rather than a literal clock time ('N candles earlier/later', 1-min candles so N candles = N minutes) gives 10 of 12 comparable cards pointing the same direction (engine late). Combined n=10 late: median -6.5 min, mean -12.2 min, range -58 to -1.
claims.austin_quote: a entry wrong, b candle right but entry is 3 candles earlier
claims.codeable_form: Same as above but also parse notes text for the pattern '(\d+) candles? (earlier|later)' and apply that offset (in minutes, assuming 1-min bars) to the row's engine timestamp field. UBER_2025-10-21: dot_B_et 10:24, '3 candles earlier' -> -3. SPCX_2026-08-03: setup_et 09:44, '3 candles earlie[r]' -> -3. PLTR_2024-09-20 (trade_anatomy): et 10:11, 'entry shouldve been 6 candles earlier' -> -6. n_relevant=12 is every row in either file where he named ANY comparable minute or candle-offset alongside an engine timestamp (the full denominator for this axis's minute-level claims).

claims.claim: "As candle forming" (or CAPS variants) appears 11 times across the two files and is used consistently to mean an intrabar fill during the signal candle's formation, not waiting for that candle's close — corroborating the zero-tolerance limit-at-the-level finding already logged in CLAUDE.md (g87/g88). One card makes the close-vs-forming contrast explicit and even notes that a clean candle-close entry is sometimes fine.
claims.austin_quote: AS CANDLE FORMING, see on that candle close you get a bad entry? and its hard to enter a stock when there 2 stop loss options and you wouldve stayed in the trade if you went with the OCR entry 6 candles later.
claims.codeable_form: NOT-CODEABLE AS A TIMESTAMP RULE DIRECTLY — but codeable as a fill-mode flag: entry_fill_mode = 'intrabar_limit_at_level' (fires while the signal candle is still open, at the level, per the already-shipped zero-tolerance limit finding) vs current 'candle_close' mode. n_relevant=88 is every card in the two files where he named ANY specific entry minute at all (the pool where this phrase could plausibly have appeared); it appeared in 11 of those. Within the 11 uses, meaning is 11/11 consistent (no card uses the phrase to mean anything other than an intrabar/pre-close fill), which is why the claim on MEANING is rated strong despite the low base rate of the phrase itself.

claims.claim: Two distinct complaints exist and are not the same thing: (a) pure lateness on an otherwise-correct signal/candle, and (b) the engine anchoring to the BREAK candle instead of the RETEST (OCR) candle — a structural/mechanism complaint, not just a minute-count complaint. UBER_2025-10-21 proves they're separable ('b candle right but entry is 3 candles earlier' = correct candle, wrong minute only). The mentor-ballot note on rule_03 explicitly frames (a) as a symptom of (b): lateness is called a bug whose fix is entering during the retest.
claims.austin_quote: sounds like the same thing i always say, but engine entering late is a bug, should always be entering while the restest is occuring, just always need that displacement for S trades
claims.codeable_form: Two separate flags on each graded miss: is_late (entry_et later than Austin's named/offset minute) and is_break_not_retest (Austin's notes name 'break'/'break candle'/'no break and retest' as the reason, i.e. the engine anchored its entry to the initial level-break bar rather than the subsequent retest/OCR bar). Only 6 of the 34 timestamp-bearing cards name the break-vs-retest mechanism explicitly, so this is a hint on cause, not a settled rule; UBER_2025-10-21 is the cleanest case showing lateness can occur with NO break/retest complaint (pure timing miss on a correctly identified retest), so the two flags must stay independent, not collapsed into one.

claims.claim: No card in either file has Austin saying the engine entered too early on a signal he agreed was valid. Of the 12 comparable cards, the only two with a positive (engine-earlier) delta are not true 'too early' complaints: COIN_2026-07-24 answers a different question (when displacement/confirmation happened, not his preferred entry) and PLTR_2024-10-23 is a break-vs-retest complaint (he wants the LATER retest candle instead of the engine's earlier break candle) — the asymmetry (engine late, never early) holds for every card where he actually states an entry preference.
claims.austin_quote: displaced and closed into the levels at 9:45, but these past 8 make me anxious you cant remember what it means
claims.codeable_form: NOT-CODEABLE as a positive rule (absence of evidence, not a rule to encode) — but usable as a guardrail: any future 'engine too early' claim must be checked against whether the miss is (a) a genuine preferred-entry-earlier-than-engine statement, versus (b) a displacement/confirmation-timing note or (c) a break-vs-retest structural note, before it's counted, because both of the only two positive-delta cards found here were (b) or (c), not (a).

unsupported_questions: Is the engine's lateness ALWAYS caused by anchoring to the break candle instead of the retest (as rule_03 claims), or are there independent, unexplained-cause late entries? MSFT_2026-08-10, SOFI_2025-11-07, GOOGL_2024-10-15 and QQQ_2025-02-25 show clear lateness with no break/retest language at all in the note — the marks can't settle whether that's because the cause genuinely differs or because he just didn't bother restating a rule he'd already stated elsewhere.

Does 'as candle forming' mean a limit resting at the level for every setup, or only for some (BABA_2026-05-06 says candle-close entries are sometimes fine and 'look cleaner')? The 11 cards don't establish which setups tolerate a close-wait and which require the intrabar fill.

Are the 1-to-58-minute strict deltas (n=7) and the 3-minute 'N candles' deltas (n=4) really the same underlying phenomenon at different scales, or is the 58-minute SOFI outlier a different failure mode (e.g. the engine missing an early setup entirely and only firing on a much later, unrelated one)? The marks give the number but not the mechanism.

Do these 1-minute candle assumptions (used to convert 'N candles earlier' into minutes) hold across all decks reviewed here, or does any deck use a different bar timeframe that would change the candle-to-minute conversion?

Is the true base rate of the 'as candle forming' entry style higher than 11/88 suggests, given that many of the other 77 minute-naming cards may simply not have needed to distinguish forming-vs-close because the question asked (e.g. 'which signal', 'where is the stop') didn't call for it?

decoded.headline: "Chop" fires in 15/22 (68%) of his structured refusals and is entangled with "level_not_respected" (co-occurs in 8 of the 9 level_not_respected cards) rather than being an independent reason — but the free text shows "chop" is at least 3-4 distinct chart states his checkbox conflates into one word, and neither "exhausted" (candle count) nor "late" (wall-clock time) has a threshold anywhere in the corpus.

No ENTRY_REJECTED or equivalent no-trade/entry-timing classifier exists anywhere in signal_runner.py.

But the codeable_form itself is entirely unbuilt — there is no stop_pick=='none' branch anywhere to check against, so this is a green-field proposal, not a partially-wired rule.

groundings.claim: Claim 2: where he states a stop rationale, the stop is pinned to a structural anchor (candle entered on, opening-range candle body, or pivot structure), never a standalone fixed-distance offset — codeable_form: stop_price = structural_anchor_price(entry_candle_body_extreme | opening_range_candle_body_extreme | nearest_pivot).
groundings.evidence: signal_runner.py:1536-1568 `placed_stop()` implements exactly this family of anchors behind the STOP_PLACEMENT flag (STOP_PLACEMENTS tuple at line 1139: 'entry_bar','candle_entered','ocr_wick','broken_level','routed'). 'candle_entered' -> stop = candle.low/high (line 1552-1553); 'broken_level' -> stop = level_stop (the broken structural level); 'ocr_wick' -> the OCR candle's far wick (order_block_wick_stop, line ~1520-1533); 'routed' sends BREAK_AND_RETEST to the level and ONE_CANDLE_RULE to the OCR wick (lines 1558-1565). Pivot structure feeds the same B&R path as named levels via pivot_levels()/T10 (lines 1445-1490, 2779-2794), so 'nearest pivot' is also a real structural stop input. This is a fixed-distance-free, anchor-based model exactly as the claim describes -- BUT it is gated behind an env flag (default STOP_PLACEMENT='entry_bar', which returns the detector's own structural_stop unchanged) and is NOT the shipped default path; and every anchor used is the candle's low/high (wick extreme), never open/close (body) -- 'candle_entered' uses candle.low/candle.high, not a body price. grep for '.body'/'candle.open' as a stop reference in signal_runner.py returns zero hits.
groundings.note: The mechanism the claim wants (structural-anchor stop, not fixed-offset) already exists and is wired end-to-end (min-risk floor, R denominator, no-repeat key per the T24 comment). The gap to close for shipping is just flipping/routing STOP_PLACEMENT, not building new logic. But note the claim's own phrase 'opening-range candle body' is imprecise against the code: the implementation is wick-extreme (low/high), not body (open/close) -- worth flagging since claim 4 (same axis) separately surfaces Austin saying 'i dont like bodies,' which is actually consistent with the code using wicks, not in tension with it as claim 4's own text suggests.

The claim's second, corroborating factor DOES exist: `level_not_respected()` in research/downgrade.py:243-249 is a real, wired downgrade factor ('candles CLOSING AT the level, or chopping on it, instead of reacting off it') feeding score() at line 500+, which floors the S/A/C grade -- so the 'level not respected' half of the META_2024-09-30 combo is codeable and already coded as a downgrade input; only the 'two stop options' half is unimplemented.

This is genuinely new logic, not a dead branch.

groundings.claim: A simpler 2-scale pattern: scale at HOD, stop BE-or-hold, second scale on revisit to the HOD area, stop remainder at BE.
groundings.evidence: RULE6_ENABLED (backtest_week.py:128-136) is the only 'scale-then-BE' code, and it is (a) a SINGLE scale at entry+-1R, not at HOD, (b) OFF by default per a 12mo A/B synthesis, and (c) has no 'revisit the level' second rung -- _ladder_bar (lines 642-736) checks scale_level once (`_target_hit` -> t.scaled=True) and never re-arms a second partial. No 'revisit'/re-touch logic exists in the file.
groundings.note: Confirms the claim's own single-card caveat -- nothing in the codebase generalizes this pattern beyond RULE6's already-shelved single scale.

groundings.claim: The raw 2R target is overridden by an HTF level or whole psych-dollar number when one sits close to 2R.
groundings.evidence: Two separate, uncoordinated mechanisms exist, neither matching the claimed 'close-to-2R override': (1) signal_runner.py blocking_levels()/_grade_for_levels() (lines 1696-1710, 2036-2065) finds levels inside the entry-to-2R path and DOWNGRADES the trade to grade C (MESH_S_VETO/LEVEL_BLOCK_CAP) -- it does not retarget. It stamps sig['path_target'] as future-target-policy metadata ('R25... is what a level-first target policy takes'), but grep confirms path_target/path_levels are never read anywhere else in the shipped tree -- dead metadata. (2) backtest_week.py's runner_target ladder (lines 1032-1043) UNCONDITIONALLY replaces the blind-2R idea with the nearest PDH/PMH/whole-dollar level beyond the scale point for every scaled trade -- there is no proximity/closeness check to the 2R price anywhere, and no CLOSE_THRESHOLD constant exists in the codebase.
groundings.note: Confirms the codeable_form's own flag that CLOSE_THRESHOLD is unquantified, and goes further: no threshold concept of any kind is wired in -- one path is a grade-cap, the other is an unconditional level substitution.

groundings.claim: Scale-size split (30/30/30/10 vs 50/20/10/10) should be conditional on whether the day is trending.
groundings.evidence: No variable split exists anywhere. RULE6_SCALE_PCT is a flat 0.5 constant (backtest_week.py:133); the F1 ladder's pnl() hardcodes '0.5 * scale_r + 0.5 * run_r' (line 397-402) -- always 50/50, two legs, never three or four. daily_trend_bias() (signal_runner.py:1862) exists but only feeds HTF_BIAS_GATE (a signal-veto, bullish/bearish/neutral), never a size-split decision; downgrade.py's counter_trend_not_respected() is likewise a grade check, not a split selector.
groundings.note: Would need a new N-way split model plus a trending classifier repurposed from daily_trend_bias(), and rewiring pnl() off its fixed 0.5/0.5.

groundings.claim: 'be' wrong co-occurs with 'entry' wrong in 2/3 cards, suggesting mistimed entry cascades into mistimed BE since BE is set relative to entry price.
groundings.evidence: No code measures or asserts this correlation -- it's a 3-card corpus observation. The structural premise is real in code, though: be_level in backtest_week.py (RULE6, ~line 1024) and the BE_TRIGGER='pt1'/'mfe' stop-raise (lines 180-192, 668-693) are both computed as offsets from sig['entry'], so an entry-timing error would mechanically shift the BE level too -- consistent with, but not proof of, the claim.
groundings.note: The claim itself stays correlational/not-codeable as written; only the entry-dependency premise is code-confirmed.

groundings.claim: The runner leg lands closer to entry than the 2R target when it should sit past 2R by construction, and its realized R-multiple (~0.41R) undershoots the stated mean RR of 2.5.
groundings.evidence: Confirmed live bug, unguarded. backtest_week.py runner_tgt (lines 1032-1043) is computed purely as 'nearest PDH/PMH/whole-dollar level beyond the scale (HOD/LOD) point' -- it never compares against t.target (the 2R price computed separately at ~line 1024). Since scale_level can be only a small fraction of a risk unit away from entry (whatever the day's HOD is as-of the signal bar) and the whole-dollar fallback is just the next $1 level, runner_tgt routinely lands well inside the entry-to-2R distance -- exactly Austin's complaint. pnl() (lines 396-402) uses t.scale_level and t.exit_price directly and never checks runner distance against target at all, so nothing in the code prevents or even flags this. Separately, options_sizer.py:37 does carry `DEFAULT_RR = 2.5` as a target ratio, but it is not wired as a check against any realized runner R-multiple anywhere in backtest_week.py.
groundings.note: A guard (`assert/clamp: runner_tgt beyond target`) is a small code change; deciding the actual desired policy (always push runner past 2R vs. accept a closer real level) is Austin's call, not an engineering one.

groundings.claim: HTF 1h/4h pivot structures should be the basis for scaling targets (independently named in the wider corpus).
groundings.evidence: pivot_levels() (signal_runner.py:1445-1488) computes swing pivots on the SAME intraday candle series the signal trades on -- not resampled to 1h/4h -- and feeds the MESH S-veto / rule10 noise-count, never the exit ladder. backtest_week.py does fetch 1h bars (yf.download(..., interval='1h'), line 813) but only for htf_bias_for(), a bullish/bearish/neutral GATE, not a level source; no 4h data is fetched anywhere in the repo for any purpose.
groundings.note: 1h bars are already in hand for bias; turning them into pivot levels and wiring those into runner_tgt's candidate list is a bounded extension. 4h would need new data plumbing first.

groundings.claim: Base rate: 35/60 (58.3%) S on the deep_is_s deck, not the live selectivity target.
groundings.evidence: No code computes or asserts this ratio. It is a mark-file/deck statistic, not a rule signal_runner.py, stop_rule.py, backtest_2y.py or downgrade.py implements. research/downgrade.py exists precisely because deck-level S-rate framing was rejected in favor of a per-signal S/A/C score (score = tripped - confluence, floored at C) that is measured against the whole 2-year book, not a pre-filtered 60-card deck. The claim's own caveat (don't treat this as engine selectivity) is consistent with how the code is actually structured -- there is no single 'selectivity' constant to check it against.
groundings.note: Not a code-groundable rule; it's a corpus statistic. Fine as measured context, nothing to implement or contradict.

groundings.claim: Chop (non-monotonic candle alternation at the level) is a veto for S.
groundings.evidence: research/downgrade.py:243-248 `level_not_respected()` is the closest code analogue ('candles CLOSING AT the level, or chopping on it... instead of reacting off it', CHOP_TOUCHES=2 closes within 0.25*ATR of the level). But it is explicitly NOT a veto: score() (downgrade.py:500-567) sums it into `tripped`, and net = tripped - confluence is floored at C, never auto-skipped -- the docstring (downgrade.py:17-21) says the old hard-veto mechanism (`TradeGrade.D`) was killed at Austin's own request ('nothing is auto-skipped by candle shape ever again'). Worse: signal_runner.py:717 records that a 2026-08-28 re-measurement (`w9_downgrade_signs.md`) found `level_not_respected` is WRONG-SIGNED -- it fires on 62.7% of the book and tripped trades outperform clean ones (+1.0046R n=640 vs +0.8711R n=377), i.e. treating it as a reason to reject actively marks BETTER trades worse in the measured data. Additionally downgrade.py is not wired into the live engine at all (ENABLE_DOWNGRADE_GRADER defaults 0, signal_runner.py:610-620), so even as a soft downgrade it has zero effect on what currently trades.
groundings.note: If this claim is used to justify a hard chop veto, that is the exact bug class CLAUDE.md warns about in reverse -- a real rule (Austin says chop) got encoded once, was found to be wrong-signed, and the associated hard-veto machinery was deliberately deleted. Any classifier rebuild should NOT resurrect chop as a gate without re-deriving the sign.

groundings.claim: Level-not-respected / two competing stop levels is the 2nd most common rejection reason.
groundings.evidence: Same function, research/downgrade.py:243-248 `level_not_respected`, covers 'not respecting the level' but only via closes-at-level chop counting -- it does not detect or encode 'two competing stop-loss options to choose from' at all; nothing in stop_rule.py or signal_runner.py picks between ambiguous stop levels. stop_rule.py:101-129 does implement a genuinely different 'two stops' concept (R1/R2, disaster stop tested on touch + level stop on close), which is a different mechanism entirely (risk management, not setup-selection ambiguity) and should not be conflated with this claim. Same wrong-sign and not-wired-into-engine caveats as above apply to the level_not_respected half.
groundings.note: The 'two candidate stop levels' half of this claim has no code representation anywhere in the four files -- would need new detection logic, not just re-enabling an existing flag.

groundings.claim: BR+OCR label alone is not sufficient for S (4/5 rejected).
groundings.evidence: research/downgrade.py:475-493 `has_confluence()` is exactly this: BR+OCR is a +1 that can only cancel ONE downgrade (score():549-553, `confl = confl_br_ocr or confl_ml; net = len(tripped) - (1 if confl else 0)`), never a standalone gate to S. The docstring at downgrade.py:472-474 states it outright: 'confluence: an UPGRADE, not a neutral.' signal_runner.py:839-846 (P3/G8 CONFLUENCE_SETUP_ROUTES) reiterates: it 'IS already the +1 in Austin's grade arithmetic... this ticket adds A LABEL AND A COUNT, not a gate.'
groundings.note: Code already matches this claim's codeable_form precisely -- decompose into sub-conditions rather than trust the label is exactly what has_confluence + the 8-variable score already do.

groundings.claim: BR/OCR literal-phrase confluence correlates with S but isn't required (weight, don't gate).
groundings.evidence: Same has_confluence() / score() as above. signal_runner.py:845-846 cites a matching measured effect: 'already worth +6.5 points of win rate on the 2-year book (55.8% with, 49.3% without, n=609/407)' -- i.e. the codebase already treats BR+OCR as a positive correlate worth tracking, not a gate, matching the claim's 'weight positively, do not gate' instruction almost exactly.
groundings.note: No new code needed; this claim describes behavior the scoring function already has.

groundings.claim: BR/OCR is not necessary -- pivot+wick+displacement can independently qualify as S.
groundings.evidence: downgrade.py's score() computes S whenever net<=0 regardless of confluence (downgrade.py:552-553); has_confluence is additive only, never required. So a clean signal with zero tripped downgrade variables and no BR/OCR confluence still grades S under the shipped scoring function -- structurally consistent with the claim.
groundings.note: Single-card claim strength is appropriately conservative; code doesn't need or contradict it either way, it's simply compatible.

groundings.claim: Displacement's necessity is contested; can't be a hard AND-gate.
groundings.evidence: research/downgrade.py:188-202 `no_displacement()` is one of the eight VARIABLES (downgrade.py:64-73) summed into `tripped`, not an AND-gate -- a signal with no_displacement=True but zero other trips still nets to A (one downgrade), not an auto-reject, and if confluence fires it can still net to S. This matches the claim's own codeable_form exactly (do not code as a hard AND-gate).
groundings.note: Matches the shipped design already; the claim's proposed resolution (displacement could occur earlier, at level formation) is untested in code -- no_displacement() (downgrade.py:195) measures displacement specifically on the break bar, so an 'earlier displacement' path is genuinely absent and would be new work.

groundings.claim: Entries must fire off the retest, not the break candle itself (hard rule).
groundings.evidence: detect_break_retest (imported signal_runner.py:37, referenced through 'break-and-retest' detection logic e.g. signal_runner.py:1261-1293 on retest_tol_mult) structurally requires an ordered break-then-retest sequence before a BREAK_AND_RETEST signal can fire at all -- the detector's own step 3 is a literal retest-touch check (signal_runner.py:1264, 'step 3 of detect_break_retest is `c.low <= level`'). A signal cannot exist without an intervening retest bar by construction, so entering on the break bar alone is already structurally excluded from the detector, matching the claim, even though the explicit English framing ('entering on the break is an engine error') isn't written as a standalone assertion anywhere.
groundings.note: Under-sampled in the marks per the claim, but the code-level guarantee is broader and stronger than 2 quotes -- it's baked into the detector's control flow, not an optional check.

groundings.claim: 'As candle forming' (intrabar) entries preferred over on-close even with confluence.
groundings.evidence: entry_fill.py:33-46 lists the ONLY five entry modes (published/close/next_open/chase_once/limit_level) and states 'THE DEFAULT CHANGED ON 2026-08-30... The entry is now the signal minute's CLOSE' (entry_fill.py:82, ENTRY_FILL default = 'close'). There is no intrabar / 'as candle forming' fill mode anywhere in the five -- an entry before the signal bar closes is not a representable order in the current code. This directly opposes the claim's preference for intrabar entries, and the codebase's own CLAUDE.md-documented g87/g88 sweep found the closest attempt at an earlier fill (a resting limit) had 89.6% of its fills land BEFORE the signal bar existed (look-ahead), which is why 'close' was kept as the shippable default despite being later than Austin's marks suggest he wants.
groundings.note: This is a live, acknowledged tension (not a bug) -- CLAUDE.md itself documents intraday-entry timing as an open, unresolved gap (median 24 minutes behind him) and g88's honest intrabar-limit arm ($275/day) was found not shippable. Implementing a true intrabar entry mode would need new fill-time semantics, not a flag flip.

groundings.claim: Sequencing: an earlier A/chop signal same-session predicts the day's S trade (3/3).
groundings.evidence: Related but opposite-direction machinery exists: downgrade.py:118-137 `sequence_gate()` / `ENABLE_SEQUENCE_GATE` DOWNGRADES a 2nd+ same-symbol-same-day entry (unless it's the 84%-rule re-entry) -- it penalizes lateness, it does not reward a later signal for having an earlier A/chop precede it. signal_runner.py's T14 `ARRIVAL_LADDER` (around signal_runner.py:760-800) separately tracks arrival order but as an eligibility/promotion mechanism, not a same-day-prior-signal-count feature predicting S. No code computes 'count_of_A_or_chop_signals_earlier_same_session' as a predictive feature for the next signal's grade.
groundings.note: The infrastructure to compute entry_seq per symbol-day already exists (downgrade.py's sequence_gate caller contract, downgrade.py:126-136) and could be repurposed to build this feature, but the feature itself is absent and would need new code, not a flag flip.

groundings.claim: take_the_trade=='yes' is not a clean is_s proxy (mixes in A-grade trades).
groundings.evidence: This is a claim about the marks/deck data schema (take_the_trade section vs deep_is_s section), not about signal_runner.py/stop_rule.py/backtest_2y.py/downgrade.py behavior -- none of those four files read or interpret a 'take_the_trade' field. It's a caveat for whoever builds a training pipeline off the mark corpus, not a code rule to ground.
groundings.note: Correctly out of scope for the four grounding files; nothing to confirm or contradict in code.

groundings.claim: Chop should be the primary veto bucket (checked 15/22 refusals, 68%) in a veto-reason ranker.
groundings.evidence: No standalone chop check is reachable from the engine. predicates.py:256 def is_chop_market() exists (10+ consecutive small-body candles, body/range<0.3 — Austin's own '10 or 11 chop candles' quote) but grep of signal_runner.py, backtest_week.py, backtest_2y.py, live_scanner.py, omen_bot.py finds zero references to is_chop_market/is_x_signal — it's called only by research/mark_features.py (offline feature extraction). The repo's own audit confirms this: research/g74_rescore30_score.py:410-411 MAP dict hard-codes `"chop": (None, "absent")` as an engine check. The nearest wired proxy, downgrade.py::level_not_respected, is empirically WRONG-SIGNED per the W9 sweep cited at signal_runner.py:717-724 — it fires on 62.7% of the book and correlates with BETTER trades (+1.0046R tripped vs +0.8711R clean), the opposite of a veto signal.

groundings.claim: level_not_respected co-occurs with chop 8/9 times and should be treated as a subtype of a chop veto.
groundings.evidence: The co-occurrence is partly an artifact of the instrument itself: research/g71_homework_build.py:222 and research/g75_deck2_build.py:154 both define the level_not_respected checkbox label as 'level not respected — closing on it / chopping on it', so 'chop' and 'level_not_respected' are worded as near-synonyms in the probe he's answering. Separately, downgrade.py:243-248 implements level_not_respected (>=2 closes within epsilon of the level over a 12-bar window, CHOP_TOUCHES=2) and it IS wired as an offline-measurable engine check, but signal_runner.py:717-724 documents it is wrong-signed (research/w9_downgrade_signs.md): tripped trades average +1.0046R vs clean +0.8711R. The codebase's own W9 fix ('w9c' variant, signal_runner.py:743) explicitly DROPS level_not_respected to restore a monotonic grade ladder. Strengthening its role as claimed would compound a variable the code already found backwards.

groundings.claim: Chop-state A: level-chop, price oscillating around a specific level without a decisive break, distinct from generic range chop.
groundings.evidence: predicates.py:256 is_chop_market only counts consecutive small-body candles anywhere — no level-proximity gate. downgrade.py:243-248 level_not_respected checks proximity to A specific level but not a distinct 'oscillation vs decisive break' state, and it's the wrong-signed variable noted above. No code distinguishes level-chop from generic chop.

groundings.claim: Chop-state B: post-displacement collapse — real breakout candle fires, then follow-through dies before a retest forms.
groundings.evidence: The building-block primitives exist separately: downgrade.py:188-201 no_displacement() detects a weak break bar, and downgrade.py:228-241 stale_retest() / downgrade.py:296-302 no_retest() detect a retest that's late or absent after a break. No function in downgrade.py or signal_runner.py composes 'displaced == True, then no_retest/stale_retest == True' into a single post-displacement-collapse check.

groundings.claim: Chop-state C: range/consolidation wall — price never leaves a band all morning, no breakout attempt to judge.
groundings.evidence: predicates.py:256 is_chop_market's consecutive-small-body-candle test (threshold=10) would likely fire on a genuine all-morning wall, but it never checks price containment inside a fixed high/low band — it only reads candle body/range ratios. No band-containment-since-open check exists anywhere in predicates.py, downgrade.py, or signal_runner.py.

groundings.claim: Chop-state D: trending-but-choppy — an HTF/session bias exists but no clean entry candle forms within it.
groundings.evidence: No code combines an HTF-bias read (signal_runner.py has htf_bias plumbing referenced at research/downgrade.py:500 score() signature) with a per-candle 'clean enough to enter' test. counter_trend_not_respected (downgrade.py:262-283) is the closest existing check but measures un-bought-back counter candles, not general candle inconsistency within an established trend.

groundings.claim: Chop is sometimes a downgrade rather than a hard veto (one CRM card graded yes despite a checked chop tag).
groundings.evidence: This matches downgrade.py's actual design, not an edge case. score() (downgrade.py:500+) never hard-vetoes on any single variable; it floors at grade C (research/downgrade.py:15-24, 'C is the floor... nothing below it, and nothing is auto-skipped by candle shape ever again — that was TradeGrade.D, which he asked to be removed entirely (2026-08-24)'). level_not_respected/chop-like signals only add to a downgrade COUNT (S/A/C), never an outright reject in the committed design.

groundings.claim: No repeatable candle-count threshold for 'exhausted' exists in his marks; the one numeric data point is from a different section.
groundings.evidence: downgrade.py:251-259 exhausted() is implemented, but on an entirely different unit than candle-count: it's ATR-distance from the session open (`abs(close - session_open) >= EXHAUSTED_ATR * atr`), EXHAUSTED_ATR=10.0. The module comment (downgrade.py:55-59) notes this constant was already tuned once — 3.0 was tried and rejected because it flagged every ordinary trend day as exhausted on 1-minute bars — and is still flagged 'AUSTIN HAS NOT SET' a guess. The claim's 'no candle-count number given' holds, but it's moot: the shipped proxy for exhaustion doesn't count candles at all.

groundings.claim: No hard wall-clock cutoff exists for 'late'; refusals and non-late refusals both occur in similar windows.
groundings.evidence: No LATE_HOUR/time-cutoff constant exists in signal_runner.py. The only related time gate is arrival_first = 0<=mins<=90 (signal_runner.py:2113), a GRADING-credit window (first with-trend signal of the day) not a lateness veto, applied identically whether ON or OFF (signal_runner.py:2299 comment 'late arrival not capped'). Independently, research/g74_rescore30_score.py:411 MAP dict hard-codes `"late": (None, "absent")` as an engine check, confirming this from the repo's own audit script.

groundings.claim: The deep_is_s probe section (25 refusals) carries no structured why_not tags — reasoning lives only in free-text notes.entry.
groundings.evidence: Confirmed exactly. research/g84_one_page.py render_deep() (lines 1085-1109, the deep_is_s section) builds only an 's' (S/no) question and an 'entry' free-text question — no `question("why_not", ...)` call exists there, unlike render_is_s (line 860-863) and render_take (line 1072-1075) which both include the why_not checkbox block with hb.NO_REASONS / g75b.NO_REASONS.

groundings.claim: Ambiguous stop-loss placement (2+ plausible stops) is a minor but real veto driver; unclear if the count is already computable.
groundings.evidence: It is already computable, just not live. research/g82_master_homework.py:706-725 stop_candidates() computes up to 4 distinct stop-price 'families' per entry (candle extreme, level, pivot — via signal_runner.pivot_levels, the engine's own swing/no-lookahead logic — and a disaster-% stop), and pick_stop() (line ~729) already filters to cards where all 4 disagree by more than one tolerance unit. This exists only in the offline probe-generation script (research/g82_master_homework.py) — no AMBIGUOUS_STOP flag or equivalent veto is wired into signal_runner.py's live detection path.

groundings.claim: Engine is later than Austin in all 7 literal-timestamp cases (median -10min, mean -15.1min).
groundings.evidence: entry_fill.py:82 `ENTRY_FILL = os.getenv("ENTRY_FILL", "close")` — the shipped default books every entry at the SIGNAL BAR'S OWN CLOSE (entry_fill.py:236 `if m == "close": return EntryFill(candle.close, ...)`). signal_runner.py:1391-1412 `fill_price()` delegates to this with mode='close'. Because `backtest_week` feeds the runner `candles[:i+1]` (signal_runner.py:1405-1410 docstring), the engine literally cannot react until a bar has fully closed, so any entry it books is definitionally at-or-after the close of whatever bar triggered it — structurally consistent with 'engine is always late, never early'.
groundings.note: This is deliberate, not a bug: it is the 2026-08-30 honest-fill fix (entry_fill.py module docstring) replacing the old unobtainable 'published' clamp-to-level fill. The lateness the marks describe is a real, intended consequence of that design, not a defect to patch in isolation.

groundings.claim: Adding candle-count offsets, 10/12 comparable cards show engine late (median -6.5min).
groundings.evidence: Same mechanism as above (entry_fill.py:82,236; signal_runner.py:1391-1412). Additionally for BREAK_AND_RETEST specifically, omen_bot.py:615-730 `detect_break_retest` requires an ordered break→leave→retest→CONFIRM state machine, and the CONFIRM step (omen_bot.py:627-628, enforced at 705-707) may lag the retest touch by up to `max_confirm_gap=3` bars (3 minutes on 1-min bars) before the entry candle is accepted — a second, independent source of the multi-minute lag the marks report.
groundings.note: The 3-bar confirm-gap ceiling is a tunable parameter (`max_confirm_gap`, default 3) at the detect_break_retest call sites (signal_runner.py:2810, 3112) with no override passed — worth flagging as a lever if lateness needs reducing, but changing it is a real behavior change, not a bugfix.

groundings.claim: "As candle forming" / intrabar fill at the level, corroborating a zero-tolerance limit finding — codeable as entry_fill_mode='intrabar_limit_at_level'.
groundings.evidence: entry_fill.py module docstring: 'An order cannot rest before the order exists... The signal bar itself is never scanned for a limit fill, no matter how far through the level it traded' (enforced by `_assert_causal`, entry_fill.py ~line 149-167, which raises `LookAheadError` on any bar at-or-before the signal bar). The g87/g88 zero-tolerance finding CLAUDE.md cites also only arms 'at arm_index()+1 — the first bar AFTER the setup left the level' (research/g87_retest_tol.py docstring), never inside the signal bar itself. No shipped or swept mode fires during the still-forming signal candle.
groundings.note: UNREACHABLE BRANCH FOUND, matching the CLAUDE.md bug class: signal_runner.py:2825-2831 comment claims an intrabar/mid-bar ON WATCH override ('we are in on the trigger price, mid-bar'), and fill_price() (signal_runner.py:1391-1416) always computes `close_is_bad_fill(...)` and passes it into entry_fill_price as `close_is_bad_fill=`. But entry_fill.py:211 states '`close_is_bad_fill` ONLY `published` reads it' — and `published` is not the default (`close` is, entry_fill.py:82,236). So under the shipped config, that verdict is computed on every call and silently discarded; the mid-bar override the inline comment describes cannot fire. A true intrabar-forming entry would require deliberately reintroducing look-ahead the module was built specifically to forbid — a real design decision, not a small patch.

groundings.claim: Engine anchors entries to the BREAK candle instead of the RETEST/OCR candle — a structural complaint distinct from pure lateness.
groundings.evidence: omen_bot.py:615-730 `detect_break_retest`'s FSM already anchors the entry to the CONFIRM candle (the one that closes back through the level, within `max_confirm_gap` of the retest touch — omen_bot.py:626-628, 692-699, 705), not the initial BREAK candle (state 'seek_break', omen_bot.py:680-684). signal_runner.py:2830 `entry = order_fill(level_hi, current, is_long=True, ...)` prices and timestamps the trade off `current`, which at that point in the loop IS the confirm candle, not the break candle.
groundings.note: The claim's stated MECHANISM (break-candle anchoring) does not match the code, but the underlying complaint is still grounded: the real gap is retest-touch vs confirm-candle-CLOSE (up to 3 bars, priced at that candle's close per claim 1/2's mechanism), which is functionally the same lateness Austin is naming, just mislabeled as 'break vs retest' rather than 'confirm-gap + close-only fill'. Worth correcting before this becomes a codeable spec.

groundings.claim: No card shows the engine entering too early on a signal Austin agreed was valid — asymmetry (late-or-on-time, never early).
groundings.evidence: Structural corroboration, not a corpus fact to verify in code: entry_fill.py's 'close' default (line 236) always books at `candle.close` — the LAST price of the signal bar — and detection (omen_bot.py detect_break_retest, and the analogous OCR/pattern detectors) requires a full bar CLOSE to confirm (omen_bot.py:658-660, 'the CLOSE decides').
